title: Fusidic acid

indications.title: Conjunctivitis
notes: Linked prescribing pathway: conjunctivitis — Adults & children >1 month 2nd line

regimens.duration: Continue use until 48 hours after infection has cleared (typically 5-10 days)

cautions: Impaired transport and metabolism of bilirubin
Avoid contact of cream or ointment with eyes
To avoid the development of resistance, fusidic acid should not be used for longer than 10 days and local microbiology advice should be sought before using it in hospital.

interactions.description: Fusidate has been reported to cause rhabdomyolysis when given with Atorvastatin. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Fusidate has been reported to cause rhabdomyolysis when given with Fluvastatin. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Nirmatrelvir boosted with ritonavir is predicted to increase the concentration of Fusidate. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Fusidate has been reported to cause rhabdomyolysis when given with Pravastatin. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Fusidate has been reported to cause rhabdomyolysis when given with Rosuvastatin. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Fusidate has been reported to cause rhabdomyolysis when given with Simvastatin. Manufacturer advises avoid.

effects: Appetite decreased; asthenia; headache; malaise; rash pustular; rhabdomyolysis
Dry eye; eye discomfort; vision blurred
Dizziness; drowsiness; hepatic disorders; hyperbilirubinaemia; thrombophlebitis; vascular pain (reduced if given via central vein)
Diarrhoea; dizziness; drowsiness; gastrointestinal discomfort; nausea; vomiting
Agranulocytosis; anaemia; leucopenia; neutropenia; pancytopenia; renal failure; rhabdomyolysis; thrombocytopenia
Agranulocytosis; anaemia; hepatic disorders; hyperbilirubinaemia; leucopenia; neutropenia; pancytopenia; renal failure; thrombocytopenia

pregnancyBreastfeeding: Not known to be harmful; manufacturer advises use only if potential benefit outweighs risk.
practicalPoints: Manufacturer advises monitor liver function with high doses or on prolonged therapy; monitoring also advised for patients with biliary tract obstruction, those taking potentially hepatotoxic medication, or those taking concurrent medication with a similar excretion pathway.

Manufacturer advises for intravenous infusion , give intermittently in Sodium Chloride 0.9% or Glucose 5%; reconstitute each vial with 10 mL buffer solution, then add contents of vial to 500 mL infusion fluid to give a solution containing approximately 1 mg/mL. Give requisite dose via a central line over 2 hours (give over at least 6 hours if administered via a large peripheral vein).
